dedupe_keys.name: entso e expert panel final report on the 28 april 2025 blackout in continental spain and portugal

description: This case study is the final report of the ENTSO-E Expert Panel on the total blackout of continental Spain and Portugal at 12:33 CEST on 28 April 2025, the most severe blackout on the European system in over 20 years, which also briefly disrupted a small area of southwest France. The panel of 49 members, drawn from transmission operators, Regional Coordination Centres, ACER and national regulators and chaired by experts from two unaffected operators, was set up on 12 May 2025 under the system operation guideline and the Incident Classification Scale methodology, met sixteen times and published its report on 20 March 2026 after a data collection and factual phase followed by root cause analysis. It finds a combination of oscillations, voltage and reactive power control gaps, different voltage regulation practices, rapid output reductions and generator disconnections in Spain, and uneven stabilisation, and sets recommendations for operations, monitoring, data exchange and regulation. Access: the report is downloaded from the ENTSO-E page for free, with no licence stated. Caveats: a regulatory investigation report, not a simulation model, and the page shows no measurement data files. It suits validation of cascading failure and voltage stability studies and resilience planning, and relates to the Texas 2021 winter storm blackout case study catalogued here.

name: ENTSO-E Expert Panel final report on the 28 April 2025 blackout in continental Spain and Portugal
outcomes: Blackout resulted from many interacting factors: oscillations, gaps in voltage and reactive power control, differing voltage regulation practices, rapid output reductions and generator disconnections in Spain, and uneven stabilisation capabilities, causing fast voltage rises and cascading disconnections. Recommendations cover operational practice, monitoring and data exchange, and regulatory adaptation.
